subject: Re: Cold-room release signoff cascade and image expiry policy
messages:
From: David Park <david.park@glacierdefense.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: Cold-room release flow, signing cascade & image expiry

Mina / Redwood team,

Thanks for the call earlier this week. As discussed, Glacier Defense is preparing to accept the first sealed-bundle deliveries into our cold-room environment. Before we lock calendars for the operator handover, we need a clear CR (custody & release) process from Redwood that covers:

- How release artifacts are signed and which signatures are required for activation (primary signer, quorum thresholds, secondary operator).
- How images are cataloged and an expiry/rotation policy so we don't inadvertently reintroduce stale images.
- Expected timelines for signed bundle delivery and a sample acceptance checklist for our on-site operators.

Can you share a concise flow doc and the signing matrix you expect operators to verify on delivery? Also: does Redwood support time-bound activation tokens (i.e., signed manifests that expire) so the Glacier operator cannot install older, revoked bundles?

We'd like to target a dry-run acceptance the week of Jan 19 — that gives us time to review your docs and raise any SOC/audit questions.

Attached: a short spreadsheet with our proposed acceptance fields (glacier-ma-qa-checklist.xlsx).

Thanks,
David Park\Engineering Program Manager\Glacier Defense

---
Attachment: glacier-ma-qa-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 24KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: David Park <david.park@glacierdefense.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Cold-room release flow, signing cascade & image expiry

David —

Thanks for the clear list. I've sketched a compact release flow and an initial signing cascade; dropping both here for review. High level:

1) Build & sign: Redwood build service produces artifact -> primary build key (redwood-release@kms) signs manifest.
2) Cross-sign: Two independent approvers (security lead + product lead) countersign the manifest. Countersignatures are required for any cold-room activation.
3) Courier & ingest: Manifest travels with sealed media; operator verifies signatures against the signing-matrix at handoff.
4) Activation window: Signed manifest includes an activation window (start_ts / expiry_ts). If activation is attempted outside the window, the runtime rejects activation and operators must request a fresh manifest.

Key decisions we want from Glacier: quorum (2-of-3 vs 3-of-4), expiry window defaults (we suggest 72 hours for dry-run, 7 days for production), and whether you require a separate in-country auditor sign-off for each delivery.

I've attached: signing-matrix-v1.pdf (matrix + checklist) and a short draft policy for image expiry (image-expiry-policy-draft.md).

If that looks good, Karthik and I will update the DocuSign flow and produce the operator-facing acceptance checklist.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad\Program Manager, Private Deployments\Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Cold-room release flow, signing cascade & image expiry

Mina —

This looks pragmatic and covers most of our audit concerns. A few clarifications before we confirm the Jan 19 dry-run: 

- Quorum: Glacier prefers a 3-of-4 model for production deliveries (to include an independent auditor key). For dry-run we can accept your suggested 2-of-3.
- Expiry: 72 hours for the dry-run is fine; for production we'll want 48 hours for activation to reduce replay risk.
- Time sources: must you rely on a network time source at activation? Our cold-room has no NTP; we need a signed manifest that validates purely against embedded timestamps, not against a live clock.

Also: can the manifest contain a SHA256 chain of the signed images plus a human-readable shortname (bundle-20260119-glacier-v1) so our operators can quickly scan the manifest during handoff?

If Redwood can confirm the 2/3 dry-run flow, provide a POA (point-of-contact) for the operator day (name + mobile) and the final operator checklist PDF, we'll lock the dry-run slot.

Regards,
David

Thanks — got it. Short answers and next steps: 

- Quorum: We will run the dry-run as 2-of-3 (build signer + security + product). Production default will be 3-of-4; we'll add an auditor key for Glacier if you provide the auditor public key to our onboarding key roster.

- Expiry & time validation: We support offline validation against embedded timestamps. Manifests include start_ts and expiry_ts and a signed ttl. The activation code path checks the manifest timestamps locally (no NTP required). We will document how to set operator clocks for the acceptance window if you choose to rely on local monotonic time.

- Manifest content: We will include a compact SHA256 list and a shortname in the manifest. Example manifest id: bundle-20260119-glacier-v1 (we'll redact full SHAs in operator-facing docs and provide them in the acceptance spreadsheet).

- POC for the dry-run operator day: Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.com, +1-415-555-0192). He will be on-site (remote ops line) for the handoff and will run the acceptance checklist.

Next steps (action items):
1) Redwood: update signing-matrix to 2-of-3 for dry-run and generate operator-checklist PDF (target Jan 14).
2) Glacier: confirm auditor public key (if you want 3-of-4 for production) and confirm dry-run acceptance team.
3) Both: schedule dry-run for Jan 19 and exchange secure courier details.

I'll attach the operator checklist draft once Karthik signs off internally. Laura, tagging you for any legal/PO concerns on auditor key insertion.

Best,
Mina Haddad\Program Manager, Private Deployments\Redwood Inference
